News.title: Girls aged 11 sold to be ‘raped by 60 men a day’ & boys raised to become ‘Romeo’ pimps… inside ‘sex slave capital’
News.content:
UNIMAGINABLE 20-hour rape ordeals, girls as young as 11 sold into the sex trade, and boys groomed into becoming ‘Romeo’ pimps from the age of five – this is the grim reality for those in the world’s depraved “sex slavery capital”.

Here, thousands of teen girls are wooed by men with the promise of plush mansions and a better life before being sold into prostitution. They are captured, enslaved and raped until they “disappear” when they are no longer useful. Now, a brave survivor tells The Sun about the horrors she endured – and campaigners reveal how it’s virtually impossible to stop.



At just 14 years old, Sophia* met her 17-year-old pimp at a local park, who showered her with affection. Being poor and neglected by her family, Sophia fell in love with Jose, who promised her a real home and a real family.



But she had no idea he would sell her body to hundreds of men and leave her to be relentlessly raped for 20 hours every day for three years.

It was in Mexico City where Sophia was first lured in before being brought to Tenancingo, the impoverished town in the state of Tlaxcala that is known as Mexico’s sex trafficking capital.

When she arrived, she says she had no idea where she was but didn’t ask any questions – worried her dreams of a happier life would be ruined if she spoke out.

Sophia was introduced to Jose’s family, who agreed she could stay if she worked on the farm and in the fields. She believed she had found a safe place to live.

In reality, the land – made up of several houses – was controlled by pimps. Some were raising their own children in the same lifestyle, while other women were being exploited there in secret.



Sophia was unaware of what was happening around her and that she would soon be drawn into the same harrowing way of life.

Jose promised her a new life in America, working in a restaurant and having children and after multiple deportations and arrests, the pair finally made it to Queens, New York.

It wasn’t until later that she would finally realise that, like many other women, she’d been brought to the sex slavery capital of Tenancingo to be eventually sex-trafficked into the US.

After setting up a happy home in New York, Jose revealed his true identity, and Sophia was turned into a sex slave.

He had been brought up as a pimp from a young age and was a master of the methodical process of grooming, Sophia says.



He tried to persuade Sophia that the money from selling her body would be worth it, saying: “You’re undocumented here; this is all you can do. This is all you have. You love me. You would do anything for me.”

Sophia attempted to escape several times but was punished by Jose, who broke her jaw on one occasion to “teach a lesson”, while another captor threatened to kill her and her family, who were unaware of what was happening across the border.

She says: “I couldn’t comprehend what was going on. I had no other options but to live like this.”

At times, Sophia says she would be forced to have sex with at least 35 men and women in one day. They would torture her body to the point where she still has injuries years later.

Holding a gun to her head, Sophia says one buyer raped her and spat the words “you’re a prostitute”.



She adds: “I was just a child. I was forced into sex trafficking.”

Tenancingo sits in the financially crippled corner of Tlaxcala, where exploitation is a way of life, and trafficking isn’t a secret – it’s a disturbing trade that brings in millions.

Here, thousands of girls are still being tricked with the same persuasive narratives – only to be captured, enslaved and raped until they’re no longer useful so they “disappear”.

Typically, the best-looking male recruits – dubbed “Romeos” – are deployed to approach girls as young as 11 to lure them into their sick world.

Campaigner and protection lawyer, Lori claims: “One girl was trafficked so young she didn’t even know how old she was. The younger the victim, the more profitable.”



Victim Sophia says captors even try to get the young girls pregnant. If a woman has a child by the pimp, it can be held hostage for years, so the mother would never run away. Women who become pregnant by other men are often killed, too, shocking reports suggest.

In vulnerable regions, parents are sometimes bribed with goods in trade for their daughter to become a sex slave. Camilla, a police officer from Tenancingo, told the Times: “Parents in these [poor] areas trade them for a bottle of wine or a sack of food.”

Angelo Kevin Brown, a criminology professor and former UN researcher, says Tenancingo is understood to be the main capital area for sex trafficked women in the country and potentially in the world.

Out of a population of roughly 10,000, local charities estimate that up to 1,000 residents are active traffickers or pimps who control over 9,000 women globally.



Karla Jancito Romero, 32, another survivor, told The Sun she was raped thousands of times by the age of 16.

Groomed from the age of 12 in her home town, Tenancingo, she said she was “vulnerable, confused and searching for love” when she first met Oscar, describing him as her “prince charming”.



Karla agreed to move to Puebla, near Mexico City, with Oscar to “escape the violence and pain” her family inflicted on her for years.

Sexual abuse was always a part of Karla’s life back at home, she said. When Oscar came into her life, the “fear loneliness and pain” from family life began to fizzle out.

When she arrived, she was faced with the realisation that her “Romeo” was a pimp who, she says, forced her to sleep with 30 men a day in brothels, motels, and on the streets.

“Some men would laugh at me because I was crying,” Karla said. “I had to close my eyes so that I wouldn’t see what they were doing to me.”

After a customer gave her a lovebite, she claims her trafficker punched, kicked and spat on her – and then burned her with an iron.



Karla said: “I was only a child trying to survive. I did not understand the dangers around me or how my vulnerabilities could be used against me.”

After enduring three-and-a-half years as a sex slave, Sophia finally built up the courage to escape, calling a taxi and racing to the police station.

When she arrived, the officers told her: “You are not the only person who has come to us.”

That was when Sophia met Lori, who had twice travelled to Tenancingo.

Lori told The Sun that a Tenancingo pimp can earn $500,000 (£373,000) a year from three women trafficked to the US.



Clients hand over around $35 for 15 minutes, with some victims reportedly forced to endure being raped by up to 60 men a day.

Lori Cohen, the CEO of Protect All Children from Trafficking, said: “Girls are dying because of this. There’s choking, stabbing, breaking of ribs, punching and kicking.

“It was as if they purchased the right to inflict as much pain as they could within that 15-minute time period.”



Visiting the barren, overgrown outskirts of Tenancingo, Lori said it was a place filled with dilapidated motels advertising girls for sale along the highway and “dozens” of flashy mansions used to lure in women.

The properties are partly used as status symbols to attract unsuspecting victims.

The unlikely crime hub traces back to the 1950s, when industrialisation left workers with few options beyond low-paid factory jobs.

Many saw how the lucrative sex trade was working in neighbouring states and brought the trade home.

The industry is typically run by family-operated rings, with approximately 3,000 traffickers known as “padrotes” – the Spanish name for pimps.



“Men usually follow in their father’s footsteps to be involved in managing and exploiting vulnerable girls,” Dr Brown said.

One local from Tenancingo told The Sun: “I have a lot of family that are in the business. It’s just like the norm over here.”

Lori said boys are often “groomed to be pimps from the moment they’re born. Their value is how many girls they can recruit and how many girls they can control.”

One in five children wants to be a pimp when they grow up, according to a 2010 University of Tlaxcala study. Even grandmothers have been identified as masterminds of warped child trafficking rings.

Consuelo Carreto Valencia was part of a ruthless family-run sex trafficking ring that stretched from Mexico to New York – cashing in on the exploitation of vulnerable young women.



The so-called matriarch, who worked alongside her sons and relatives, was handed more than 10 years behind bars after she profited from a scheme that lured girls to the US before forcing them into prostitution.

The victims were shipped into brothels across Queens and Brooklyn – cut off from their families and left with almost nothing.

Meanwhile, the Carreto clan raked in hundreds of thousands of dollars from their suffering, and the grandma was the mastermind behind the entire operation.

Lori said: “You just see this tiny lady who looks utterly harmless, and you realise she’s running a major crime syndicate.”

Professor Brown, the UN researcher, said cash-strapped cops are bribed by pimps, leaving them “highly incentivised” to take backhanders.



He added: “Despite the clear knowledge of sex trafficking here, it is rarely investigated by the police.”

In Karla’s case, her hopes of being saved before her escape were dashed when she claimed police raided a brothel where she was working, but then filmed the girls in compromising positions.

Lori claims there is a “tremendous amount of corruption at a local level,” with even mayors, prosecutors and judges involved in the trafficking of girls.

She said: “It generates tremendous wealth – and with that wealth comes tremendous power and impunity.”

In Tenancingo, the booming sex trade industry employs most of the town’s 10,000 residents.



Over time, networks have expanded and hardened, with some of the most powerful families in the town now believed to have links to Mexico’s most feared cartels.

Mexico is facing a wider crisis, with more than 130,000 people vanishing without a trace over the last two decades, many feared abducted or killed by organised crime groups.

Official figures show that around ten women and girls are murdered every day, a toll that has risen steadily over the past 20 years.

The female homicide rate was at a staggering 3,928 in 2022. Dr Brown said: “Many of the girls who try to get out end up killed.

In recent years, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) has tightened its grip, taking a cut from pimps and driving profits higher.



With demand surging, violence has escalated.

Experts say traffickers are now abandoning grooming and psychological control – instead relying on outright abduction in a brutal practice known as “guerilla pimping,” where victims are immediately forced into exploitation.

The government in Tlaxcala has told The Observer it has jailed 14 people for trafficking-related crimes since 2011, alongside 127 rescues and the closure of more than 200 bars, nightclubs and hotels.

President Claudia Sheinbaum vowed to crack down on femicide, but critics say her government has failed to properly fund protection schemes for women.

Governor Lorena Cuéllar has denied there is a sex trafficking problem – and claims it “no longer exists”.



While some traffickers have been jailed in the US, including in New York cases involving men from Tenancingo, critics say networks still operate with impunity in Mexico.

Criminal defence lawyer Michael Kruz said: “Trafficking charges almost never reach the people actually running the operation.

“The structure of these networks is designed so that evidence collected produces nothing that points upward toward leadership.

“The legal system keeps engaging the bottom of these networks while the people running them remain untouched.”

*Some of the names in this article have been changed.

News.title: Seven dead and over 100 injured after huge indigenous brawl breaks out with rivals fighting with sticks and stones
News.content:
AT least seven people have died and over 100 have been left injured after a massive indigenous brawl between rival communities.

Jaw-dropping footage showed the sprawling clash involving rifles and stones erupt due to a years-long feud over land rights in Colombia.





The Misak and Nasa communities battled in a dramatic fight in the rural Silvia region – an area historically plagued by territorial disputes.

Several combatants have even been taken hostage by their opposing groups in the extraordinary fight between the two warring factions, authorities said.

At least seven people, reportedly including the leader of the Misak group Luis Enrique Tunubalá, were killed in the head-to-head battle.

More than 100 were said to have been left injured during the fierce clash.



Members from both communities used sticks and batons to attack their counterparts before moving on to rifles.

Stunning footage showed the huge 800-hectare corridor of farmland in southwestern Colombia being overrun by furious fighters.



Makeshift shields and firearms were seen used in the contest.

The Misak community accuses the Nasa group of illegally occupying the territory for months – with the former claiming it has historical ties to the region.

But the huge revolt was sparked by a government ruling that gave some recognition to Nasa over the territory.

The massive fight has sparked nationwide concern for the long-contested land.

Colombian president Gustavo Petro called for a meeting between both heads of the warring factions.



Meanwhile, the country’s vice president Francia Marquez said: “It is unacceptable that between sister communities who have endured historical state violence, exclusion, and inequality, we must resort to bloodshed to resolve our differences.

“As brother nations with shared roots and memories, it breaks my soul to see what is happening to our territory.”

News.title: Cabinet row erupts as Rachel Reeves angrily confronts Steve Reed over missing house building targets
News.content:
RACHEL Reeves furiously rounded on Steve Reed after Cabinet this week – having a pop at him over not building enough homes.

The Chancellor confronted the Housing Secretary in a “grumpy” exchange as shocked ministers watched on.



Ms Reeves is understood to have marched over to Mr Reed and told him: “Why are you not building more homes?”



The pair are then said to have had a heated exchange as they discussed government policy.

When Mr Reed said he would have to check something with his department, the Chancellor is said to have fumed: “You have been in the job for months now Steve!”

A Whitehall source said: “It looked like a heated row. Rachel marched right up to Steve and had a go.”

The dust-up happened as ministers had a cup of tea after their Cabinet meeting in Downing Street on Tuesday.



It comes amid growing fears Labour will miss their target to build 1.5 million new homes by 2029.

They could fall short by half a mission homes, experts have warned.

Labour’s ambitious housebuilding target was a key part of their plan to grow the economy.



But it has flopped on impact because of sky high energy costs, planning red tape and a shortage of trained builders.

The row erupted amid growing concerns among many Cabinet ministers that they could be sacked if Andy Burnham becomes PM.

Allies of Ms Reeves are pushing for her to stay as Chancellor – warning that bond markets could tank if she is fired by a new regime.

But most expected her to be axed from No11 if Burnham becomes PM.



Ed Miliband is lobbying for the job, but Mr Burnham may give it to a “moderate” to avoid spooking the markets.

Government sources denied the Chancellor had asked Mr Reed why more homes were not being built, but admitted there had been a set-to over housing policy.

A source close to the Housing Secretary said: “Rachel and Steve are working closely together to reach Labour’s ambitious housing target.

“As Chancellor and Housing Secretary they talk about housing issues on a regular basis.”

News.title: Moment shop owner gets locked in three-on-one scuffle with ‘shoplifter & pals after catching her  in the act’
News.content:
THIS is the moment a shopkeeper scuffled with an alleged thief – and he is now calling for a crackdown of shoplifters.

CCTV footage shows business owner Wayne Jarvis, 42, confronting an alleged shoplifter – grabbing her sleeve to try and keep her in store until the police arrived.





He is then confronted by two other men – believed to be her boyfriend and a friend – who scuffled with him before the trio managed to flee on May 8.

The shopowner had called the police – and was trying to hold back the alleged thief until they arrived. before the three fled.

She was allegedly trying pinch a greeting card worth just £1.99.

Wayne, 42, opened his shop called Fifty Scents in Worcester, West Midlands, last April.



And he says he’s already had hundreds of pounds worth of stock swiped in Britain’s shoplifting epidemic.

There were 509,566 in the UK in the year ending December 2025, a slight decrease – but the figures are still nearly 150,000 higher than pre-pandemic figures.

Wayne also added he thinks it’s “wrong” that people are losing their jobs for confronting thieves.

Morrisons manager Sean Egan was dismissed after standing up to career criminal Daniel Kendall at his store, and Waitrose worker Walker Smith was sacked after he “grabbed the bag” from a shoplifter.



Wayne said: “You shouldn’t be losing your job for that because you’re doing what is right.

“Yes, it may not be company policy to do that and let these people get away with it, but most people’s moral compass doesn’t allow that.”

Wayne is not shy about confronting wannabe shoplifters – and he’s taken to sharing CCTV of alleged offenders online in a bid to deter them.



He says his “name-and-shame” method is working – and believes it has detered thousands of pounds of thefts.

The shop owner said: “I think people need to be aware of what’s actually going on and how prevalent it is because people don’t realise what we have to put up with on a daily basis.

“People need to realise that they can’t get away with this and they can’t continue to do it. Because ultimately we’re all paying.

“It stops the repeat offenders. We’ve never caught the same person twice – they don’t ever come back”.

Surprisingly, the most popular item that gets nicked in Wayne’s store is £7.99 rubber ducks – with one lady attempting to take six of them last weekend.



CCTV footage shows Wayne in a scuffle after confronting a lifter over a £1.99 greeting card she popped in her bag before Wayne called the cops.

He said: “She obviously didn’t wanna hang around for the police and obviously started to try and escape. So I grabbed hold of a jumper to bring her back in store.

“But then obviously two other guys got involved who were, one I believe was her boyfriend and one was a friend, and they managed to eventually get her out of the store.”



“Some people say ‘all that over a £1.99 card’ – but it’s not just a card. Quite often it’s more than that.

“We stopped a lady a couple of weeks ago for a two pound bath bomb. And when she was searched, she’d got 90 pounds worth of stuff.”

The 42-year-old said shoplifting is increasing because thieves think they can get away with it – with one crook’s daughter even telling him “the police won’t do anything anyway, so why are you bothering?”.

The shopkeeper said: “Unfortunately, it does go back to the government because the prisons are full and we understand that – but you can’t keep letting people get away with stuff because it just encourages it.

“There’s no deterrent and there’s no real consequence to what they do, so they just go back out the next day and literally start doing it again.”



This comes after The Sun exclusively revealed cops gave up on 90 per cent of shoplifting cases within weeks in some areas of the UK.

And Prime Minister Kier Starmer has said he believes the “tide could be turning” on retail crime.

Speaking last month, he said the Government has put an extra 3,000 neighbourhood police officers on the streets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And he said the government had scrapped the “ridiculous” rule which left theft of goods worth less than £200 “not properly investigated” by police.

Regarding Wayne’s scuffle, a West Mercia Police spokesman said: “Enquiries are on-going into an attempted theft from Fifty Scents on Broad Street in Worcester following a report received on Friday, May 8.”

News.title: Massive chemical tank to ‘spill or explode’ at any moment in ‘unprecedented disaster’ as 40,000 evacuated from homes
News.content:
MASS evacuations have been triggered as officials brace for a huge chemical tank to spill or explode at any given time.

The 34,000-gallon tank holding methyl methacrylate (MMA) a highly flammable and volatile chemical, is located at an aerospace plant in Garden Grove, southern California.





Officials at the GKN Aerospace plant warned that it cannot be secured after it started overheating and leaking on Thursday when a relieve valve opened up to cool it down.

As a result, it now threatens to “spill between 6,000 and 7,000 gallons or explode” in what is already being called an “unprecedented disaster.”



On Friday night, emergency crews helped evacuate 40,000 Orange County residents from their homes and schools within a nine-square-mile radius of the facility as the situation worsens.

“This thing is going to fail. We don’t know when,” Orange County Fire Authority Division Chief Craig Covey warned in an emergency briefing on Friday.

As the problem spirals ever-loser to a full -blown catastrophe, officials say there are just two options left.

“One, it fails and cracks and all the product leaks out onto the ground,” Covey said.



“The other option that was told to us is that it blows up.”

“This is highly volatile, it’s highly toxic, it’s highly flammable. This is not precautionary,” he said, as residents were told to flee and 6,000 refused.

“This is gonna happen unless some brilliant guy behind me here figures out how we can mitigate this incident.”

Emergency officials and specialists from across the country are working to scramble for what Covey called an “out of the box” solution.

Responders have managed to get the tank to cool down but it is still over 10 degrees hotter than it should be and is now being constantly monitored with drones.



Sand barriers and other containment systems have been deployed to stop chemicals ending up in storm drains and waterways in the event of an explosion.

MMA vapors can cause severe respiratory issues, dizziness, nausea, and irritation to the eyes and lungs.

At extreme levels, it can spark severe respiratory distress and lead to hospitalization, local health officials warned.

“Everything will change, for sure, once this is done,” one evacuated resident who has lived in the area since childhood told the Los Angeles Times.

“We will think about moving out from there.”



“It’s been chaos,” fellow evacuee Jacqueline Riegos, from Stanton, told KCAL/KCBS.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Just dealing with everybody coming and going and nobody knows anything.

“Nobody can really give us any details about what’s going on. … And we don’t know how long this is going to be.“

News.title: E-scooter rider crashes into police officer outside Buckingham Palace as both rushed to hospital
News.content:
SCOOTER CRASH E-scooter rider crashes into police officer outside Buckingham Palace as both rushed to hospital

AN E-SCOOTER rider crashed into a police officer outside Buckingham Palace as both were rushed to hospital.

Cops cornered off the scene which left a police hat and a black e-scooter in its wake.





The crash happened yesterday at 4pm at the bottom of Constitution Hill.

Emergency services scrambled to the scene as the rider and the copper, both male, were taken to a major trauma centre.

Patrolling police were heard shouting to a cyclist “get out, you’re in a crime scene”, the BBC reports.

As the palace was not flying the Royal Standard, King Charles is thought not to have been in at the time.

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We sent an ambulance crew, incident response officer and dispatched London Air Ambulance via car to the scene.

“We treated two males at the scene and took them to a major trauma centre as a priority.”

A Met Police spokesperson added: “Both the rider of the e-scooter and the police officer were taken to hospital. Their injuries were assessed as non-life threatening and non-life changing.

“The scene of the incident was cordoned off while the level of injuries was confirmed.”

News.title: Female biology teacher accused of sexually abusing six children and ‘forced one to watch Fifty Shades of Grey’
News.content:
SICK MISS Female biology teacher accused of sexually abusing six children and ‘forced one to watch Fifty Shades of Grey’

A BIOLOGY teacher has been accused of sexually abusing six children – including allegedly forcing one girl to watch Fifty Shades of Grey.

Maris Nichols, 25, was accused of sexually assaulting the same student twice in two weeks, before she was hit further charges relating to five more teens.





Nichols is accused of telling a female victim to watch the R-rated Fifty Shades of Grey films, according to an arrest warrant seen by the Daily Mail.

The document also claimed the teacher had sex with a student in the back seat of a truck.

She is also accused of sending nudes and explicit text messages to several teenage students, including two who were under the age of 16.

Nichols also allegedly described sex acts that she desired to the teens, which the warrant said included being “choked, screamed at, slapped and whipped”.

The science teacher allegedly told one teen to delete messages she had sent him and to lie if he was questioned about any sexual abuse.

She taught biology at Alexander High School in Douglasville in Georgia.

Nichols was first accused of having sex with a pupil in a cupboard between classrooms on April 23.

She then allegedly sexually abused the same student inside a parked Hummer.



Nichols was first hired as a football operations manager at the school in April 2023 but became a Biology teacher just one month later and continued in both roles, according to her LinkedIn.

After the disturbing allegations, the school suspended Nichols and wiped her profile from their website and launched an investigation.

Nichols was first arrested on a $40,000 bond earlier this month.



The alleged abuser, who is married with one child, was bailed out, then arrested for a second time on a $74,000 bond.

In a letter to parents after the first arrest, the Douglas County School System said: “Upon learning of the alleged misconduct, the district immediately launched an investigation.

“Student safety is the district’s highest priority.

“The alleged behavior is unacceptable and violates the professional standards all employees are required to uphold”.

A concerned local parent called the horrifying allegations “heartbreaking”.



Others told 11 Alive that Nichols gave their children very little help in class, and worried that their students would fall behind.

One unnamed parent said: “‘We’re not asking for special treatment. We are asking for transparency, accountability, and fairness.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Unfortunately, our concerns have repeatedly been met with resistance, limited communication, and a lack of meaningful reassurance that appropriate measures are being taken to protect all children involved, including our own.”

Nichols faces several charges of child molestation, grooming of a minor for a sexual offence, improper sexual contact by an employee and tampering with evidence.

News.title: Inside UK’s ‘benefits city’ as workers rage jobless parents are rinsing Starmer’s handouts to ‘trot off to Disneyland’
News.content:
AS the setting for the infamous reality TV show Benefits Street, Britain’s so-called ‘second city’ has long been the face of the nation’s spiralling welfare bill.

Now, fed-up workers in Birmingham have slammed the “unsustainable” situation after Labour’s scrapping of the two-child benefits cap was accused of “giving a green light” to brazen claimants.





New analysis of the latest Department for Work and Pensions data by The Sun revealed the areas where thousands of families are now entitled to significantly more taxpayer cash following the controversial policy change, which came into force last month.

And our investigation found that Birmingham leads the pack, with 17,990 families already on Universal Credit now eligible to claim extra cash because they have three or more children.

During our visit to the West Midlands city, many hard-grafting locals said they were furious that Prime Minister Keir Starmer‘s cap-lift has only furthered the sense “it’s not worth going to work anymore”.

While some welcomed the changes – insisting it would stop them “struggling to buy food” and having to live “day-by-by” – other locals argued the system is too open to abuse, with out-of-work parents openly telling them that their large broods of kids are their “safety net”.



This attitude was brazenly endorsed by one resident from the city’s ‘Benefits Street’ – the subject of a Channel 4 reality show – who said it was claimants’ “right” to get as much as they can from “exploiting the system”.

Locals in the city – recently named both the UK’s ‘sicknote’ and unemployment capital – have long felt left behind after enduring a near-440-day bin strike, which has seen six-foot mounds of festering rubbish pile the streets and led to rats “the size of cats”.

Brummies certainly made their voices clear in the May elections, with Labour losing 48 of their 65 seat majority at Birmingham City Council. Reform UK scooped 23 of them, followed by the Greens with 19, but there remains no party majority.

Alum Rock, three miles east of the city centre, risks becoming the face of the UK’s soaring child welfare payments, due to hosting 1,154 of Birmingham’s 17,990 families that already claim Universal Credit and have three or more children.



On the suburb’s bustling high street, we met retired 999 emergency call operator John Read, 72, who was angry that “slacker parents” take such high amounts “for doing nothing”.

“It’s atrocious, topsy turvy and not sustainable,” he said. “People going to work are paying for this through taxes while they’re struggling to afford their own bills.

“I’ve got about 14 nephews and nieces. Every one one of them is a hard-working grafter, and even they are now saying, ‘It’s not worth going to work anymore’. It’s shocking.

“If people can get free money for not working, they are going to do it. It’s human nature for some people, but politicians don’t realise because they live in a Westminster bubble.”



Former Labour member John says the party now “couldn’t run a jumble sale” and are “no longer for the working man”.

“Labour is unrecognisable,” he adds. “This current lot haven’t got their hands dirty a day in their lives, they all smell of lavender and wear Savile Row suits. They don’t represent us.”

Labour’s abolition of the two-child benefits cap came into effect on April 6.

If the two-child cap hadn’t been lifted, couples this year – aged over 25, with two or more kids, and claiming benefits – would receive up to £15,299 per year or £1,274 per month.



Now able to claim for extra offspring, the capped maximum sum is £22,020 per year or £1,835 per month in Birmingham. In London, it’s capped at £25,323 per year or £2,110 per month.

Not all will take the highest sum because Universal Credit payments are means-tested and include a range of allowances including housing, childcare, health issues, disabilities and carer support.

Six miles south-west of Alum Rock in Harborne, mum-of-four Lucie, 28, told us she’s extremely grateful for the extra handouts that have seen her child benefit payments double to £1,200 per month.

It means she is no longer “struggling to buy food”, can “actually live, not live day-by-by” and no longer has to rely on her “godsend mum” for money.

Labour ministers argue abolishing the two-child cap will lift 550,000 children out of poverty by the end of the Parliament and it has certainly been a lifeline for Lucie.



She told us she couldn’t wait to get back to work but admitted not everyone is like her, with some parents “taking the mick” because it is “so easy to get benefits and not have to do anything for it”.

She added: “Some people think, now they’re getting the extra money, that’s it’s the same ‘wage’ that they would get working part-time.

“I don’t think they have the mindset of going back to work anymore. Others have said it would be easier to have another kid than work because you get more money for it.”



It’s an approach deplored by many, including a nearby electrician – who declined to be named – who warned that if some claimants are “given an inch, they will take a mile”.

He added: “The system is so easily abused, that’s the problem. I don’t agree with it.

“I’ve worked hard ever since I was a kid, while people on benefits have the life of Riley. You see them going to Disneyland with their benefits. It’s not great is it?”

Former teacher Jacky Plotnek, 74, believes child benefits are essential due to the “pockets of extreme deprivation” in Birmingham – but also thinks people should not have kids if they cannot afford them.

She said: “We’re in a nanny state now – with school meals, breakfast clubs, children not ready for school, all of these things. Parents don’t have the skills that they used to have.”



On the possible £22,000-plus earnings, Jacky added: “That could have a negative effect on the way people view parenthood. It’s detrimental and the country can’t afford it, can we?”

Similarly, retired electrician Graham Leach, 77, told us: “People are being bought up with a ‘benefits attitude’, and it has got to stop. The country doesn’t make enough money to pay the benefits out.

“They think everything comes for free but it all comes at a cost – increases in tax, council tax, national insurance.

“I don’t mind benefits as a safety net, but there are people now receiving benefits who have never paid a penny into the system.

“And unscrupulous people could be having children to get more money. In the past people were grateful for a council house, now they expect it.”



Graham’s partner, Sandra Holloway, believes the abuse of the welfare state has turned the UK into “the silliest country of all”.

The retired hairdresser, 78, told of a well-educated dad, who couldn’t get a job, feeling relieved because his five kids were “his safety net” – referring to benefit payments.

Similarly, accountant Anam Hassan, 35, who moved from Pakistan to the UK nearly four years ago, argued unemployed parents “shouldn’t become a burden on the Government”.

The mum-of-one says: “Parents should be encouraged to find work, not manipulate the Government.

“Trying to increase your family to get more benefits is cheating, it’s not fair on hard-working parents like me.”



However, on James Turner Street, known for the docuseries Benefits Street – named due to 90 per cent of the neighbourhood claiming welfare payments – some people are more forgiving.

Local Vincent Gordon told us everyone should “see what they can get” from the Government and push for as much as possible.

The long-term street resident claimed: “It’s a natural reaction, people exploiting the system, but people should try to get more if they can.

“It’s your right to try to get more and if you can’t, at least you tried… some will get away with something, some will get away with nothing.”

Nearby resident Mohammed, 34, argued the public “shouldn’t worry” about the bulging benefits bill because “more money is being wasted on wars that have nothing to do with us”.



Mohammed admits the welfare system is “not perfect” but insists children should always be the nation’s focus – because they are future taxpayers.

“I know it doesn’t look good when you’re working and see someone at home doing nothing, but no child should go hungry,” he said.

“That child, who was supported by the government welfare system, could become 10 times better than his parents were.



“If a person has five kids and claims for them, those kids will all be paying taxes in the future so they will eventually be paying the money back.”

Conservative MP Helen Whately, the Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, told us: “Labour scrapped the cap at a cost of more than £3billion a year, forcing working families to bear the cost.

“One in four workers now earn less than they’d get from welfare in Starmer’s Benefits Street Britain. Hardworking families across Birmingham know this is not fair.”

Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden said: “Children growing up in poverty are far more likely to leave school without qualifications and end up not in work or education as young adults, and we’re determined to break that cycle once and for all and give every child the best start in life.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Government spokesperson told us their Child Poverty Strategy would lift 550,000 kids out of poverty by 2030 and other welfare reforms will save “nearly £2billion by the end of the decade”.



They added: “Child poverty costs the country billions through pressure on public services and lost potential and with six in 10 of benefitting families having a parent in work, scrapping the two-child limit is an investment in Britain’s future that supports working households.”

News.title: Keir Starmer urges TNT to make Champions League final free to view
News.content:
Keir Starmer urges TNT to make Champions League final free to view

The broadcaster has reportedly irritated UEFA by opting to charge fans to watch all three European finals despite English clubs chasing a clean sweep of titles

View 2 Images PSG will be hoping to retain the Champions League (Image: Getty Images)

Keir Starmer has written to TNT sports demanding the Champions League final be broadcast on free to air.

‌



The broadcaster has reportedly irritated UEFA by opting to charge fans to watch all three European finals despite English clubs chasing a clean sweep of titles.

‌



It will be the first time since the Champions League's modern rebrand 34 years ago that viewers in the UK won't be able to watch the final without paying for a subscription.

‌



In a scathing letter, the PM said: “I was saddened to see that, for the first time since the competition started 34 years ago, TNT Sports has decided that the Champions League final will not be free to watch for football supporters here in the UK. The Champions League is the biggest club football competition in the world and rightly means a lot to fans in this country – the home of football.

UEFA fume as TNT make unprecedented Champions League final decision READ MORE :

Arsenal transfer state of play as Mikel Arteta to be handed £250m war chest READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Arsenal fan has now written to TNT Sports (Image: Tayfun Salci/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

“I am a firm believer that the final of this competition should remain free to watch, whether Arsenal have made it or not. Obviously, I want as many fellow fans as possible to be able to watch our team in this historic final for the first time in 20 years.

‌



“However, this is bigger than that. This is about supporters of all teams coming together in living rooms and pubs in every corner of the country to watch the most elite players in Europe battle it out. Hard-working people should not have to worry about forking out for a subscription to watch a game of this magnitude. We should be putting supporters first.”

Champions League finals were previously broadcast live on ITV, which had exclusive rights from the competition’s launch, as the rebranded European Cup, in 1992 until 2003, then joint rights with Sky Sports until 2015.

BT Sport acquired UEFA rights from the 2015/16 season and previously streamed European finals for free on YouTube.

‌



The channel was then rebranded to TNT Sports, which made them available for free for customers who registered with its sister streaming service discovery+ since taking over the contract two years ago.

Arsenal will look to upset holders Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final on May 30 in Budapest. The Gunners are aiming to win Europe's elite competition for the first time ever, having seen Tottenham lift the Europa League last year.

Aston Villa defeated Freiburg in the Europa League final earlier this week, and next Wednesday Crystal Palace meet Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final as they look to win a first European trophy in their history.

Article continues below

A TNT Sports spokesperson said: “It has been a privilege to bring UEFA club competitions to sports fans across the UK throughout the season. Having three Premier League clubs reach the finals shows the strength of English Football and something that we are proud to continue to support.

“We have made all three UEFA finals this year available from just £4.99, the price for a month-long subscription to HBO Max that also includes the great entertainment on the service. This represents exceptional value for fans to watch the conclusion of the competitions."

News.title: UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come
News.content:
Weather forecasting models suggest the UK could see temperatures rise to 35C as a heatwave grips the country - the Met Office has forecast 33C highs for Monday

UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come

The Met Office has confirmed the hottest day of the year so far today.

The village of Frittenden, in Kent, hit 30.3C on Saturday and the forecasting body said temperatures are still rising. Before now, Friday had seen the year's warmest temperatures when highs of 28.4C were measured in Heathrow, Cambridge and Cranwell in Lincolnshire.

It comes as the UK faces a days-long heatwave with the Met Office forecasting record breaking temperatures for May. Heat health alerts have been issued by the UKHSA across England.

The UKV weather model now suggests the East of England could reach 35C at around 3pm on Tuesday. And it shows 15 counties at 33C or more - Gloucestershire, Warwickshire, Staffordshire, Norfolk, Suffolk, Leicestershire, Northamptonshire, Cambridgeshire, Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Essex, Surrey, and Berkshire.

News.title: Ebola treatment tent in Congo set on fire as 18 suspected cases escape into community
News.content:
Ebola treatment tent in Congo set on fire as 18 suspected cases escape into community

A tent used for treating people with Ebola in eastern Congo was set on fire for the second time this week, and 18 people suspected of being infected with the Bundibugyo virus escaped into the community, a local hospital director has said

View 7 Images A fire ripped through an Ebola treatment centre in eastern Congo (Image: AP Photo/Dirole Lotsima Dieudonn)

A treatment tent used during the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo was set ablaze for the second time in a week, with 18 suspected infected individuals fleeing the scene, a local hospital director confirmed on Saturday.

‌



Unidentified individuals descended upon the clinic in Mongbwalu — a town at the epicentre of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, a rare strain of Ebola — on Friday night, torching a tent erected by humanitarian organisation Doctors Without Borders for suspected and confirmed Ebola patients, Dr Richard Lokudi, director of the Mongbwalu General Reference Hospital said.

‌



"We strongly condemn this act, as it caused panic among the staff of the Mongbwalu Referral Hospital and also resulted in the escape of 18 suspected cases into the community," he said. On Thursday, a separate treatment centre in the town of Rwampara was razed to the ground after family members were barred from reclaiming the body of a local man.

‌



View 7 Images Flames and smoke rise from the Ebola treatment center in Rwampara (Image: AP Photo/Dirole Lotsima Dieudonn)

The remains of Ebola victims are highly contagious and can trigger further transmission when families handle them for burial or gather for funeral services. Authorities are taking charge of burying suspected victims wherever possible, a move that has been met with resistance from grieving families and friends.

A burial for Ebola patients in Rwampara took place on Saturday under heavy security, as tensions between health workers and the local community reached boiling point, according to David Basima, a Red Cross team leader overseeing burials. "Arriving at the (healthcare) structure, we experienced a lot of difficulties, including resistance from young people and the community. So we were forced to alert the authorities so that they could come to our aid, just for safety," said Basima.

‌



View 7 Images Hospital beds are seen among the ruins of an Ebola treatment center (Image: AP Photo/Moses Sawasawa)

In a bid to contain the spread of the virus, authorities in north-eastern Congo imposed a ban on Friday on funeral wakes and gatherings of more than 50 people. The World Health Organization (WHO) upgraded the outbreak's risk level for Congo from "high" to "very high", though it maintained that the likelihood of the disease spreading globally remains low.

View 7 Images Sanitation workers from Bunia city government spray disinfectant in the central market area near a rubbish truck (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

‌



WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed on Friday that 82 cases and seven deaths have been verified in Congo, adding that the outbreak is thought to be "much larger."

View 7 Images A sanitation worker from the Bunia city government sprays chlorine to disinfect the central market (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

No vaccine currently exists for the Bundibugyo virus, which went undetected for weeks in Congo's Ituri province following the first known fatality, while authorities were testing for a more common strain of the Ebola virus, which returned a negative result. The number of suspected cases has now reached 750, with 177 suspected deaths, and these figures are expected to rise as surveillance efforts are broadened.

‌



View 7 Images Members of the Congo Scouts movement carry an Ebola awareness banner along a street (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

Dr Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, stressed that tackling the outbreak effectively must involve fostering trust within local communities. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies announced on Saturday that three of its volunteers had perished from the outbreak in Mongbwalu. The organisation said it suspected the three healthcare workers caught the virus while conducting dead body management activities on March 27 as part of a humanitarian mission unrelated to Ebola.

View 7 Images Motorcycle taxi riders and their passengers wait at the entrance to the central market while sanitation workers disinfect the area (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

Article continues below

This would substantially shift back the timeline of the outbreak from the earlier first confirmed death in late April in the town of Bunia, the capital of Ituri.

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor breaks cover for first time since police announced sex crime probe
News.content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor breaks cover for first time since police announced sex crime probe

Along with the investigation into misconduct in public office, detectives continue to assess reports that a woman was taken to an address in Windsor in 2010 for sexual purposes

View 4 Images The former prince was seen driving his Land Rover on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk near his new home in Wolferton, after walking his dogs this afternoon (Image: Bav Media)

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been seen for the first time since police announced they are investigating him over potential sex crimes, as part of their inquiry into potential misconduct in public office.

The former prince was seen driving his Land Rover Defender car on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk after walking his dogs this afternoon. Andrew, who was wearing a yellow shirt, had not been seen since Thames Valley Police published a new statement on Friday morning revealing the widened probe and appealing for witnesses.

Officers are said to be examining “a number of aspects of alleged misconduct” including sexual wrongdoing and corruption. The original allegations were that he gave commercially valuable information to paedophile pal Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UK’s special trade envoy from 2001 to 2011. Officers, including those specialising in sexual offences, are following several lines of inquiry in the wake of the publication of the Epstein files.

View 4 Images It is the first time Andrew has been seen since police announced they are investigating him over potential sex crimes as part of their inquiry into potential misconduct in public office (Image: Bav Media)

Andrew, 66, broke cover just hours after the Mirror revealed Buckingham Palace is “actively assisting” police with specific inquiries into allegations the former Prince Andrew committed misconduct in a public office. Sources have revealed that Thames Valley Police has asked to see visitor logs at royal residences linked to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

Detectives have also requested logs of his private protection officers, detailing their shift patterns while protecting the former Duke of York from 2001 and 2010, it is understood. It comes after police widened their inquiry to consider allegations of sexual misconduct, within their probe into potential misconduct in public office.

Mountbatten-Windsor was a special representative for international trade from 2001 to 2011, when he quit amid controversy over his friendship with sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. A source said: “Buckingham Palace is now actively assisting police inquiries, in line with the King’s statement that they stood ready to do so. This is an incredibly sensitive investigation and one in which no stone will be left unturned.”

King Charles said investigators had the family’s support and cooperation, after his brother’s arrest in February and questioning on suspicion of misconduct in public office. Mountbatten-Windsor’s former home Royal Lodge in Windsor and his then home, Wood Farm in Sandringham, were searched.

View 4 Images The former Prince Andrew, Virginia Giuffre, and Ghislaine Maxwell posing for a now infamous photo at her London townhouse (Image: US District Court - Southern Dis)

The legal definition of misconduct in a public office can include financial misconduct and sexual misconduct. Police have asked US officials for original copies of the Epstein files. They appealed for victims to come forward and are probing a woman’s claim Epstein flew her to the UK for sex with Mountbatten-Windsor in 2010.

The woman is not British and was in her 20s at the time. Her lawyer, Brad Edwards, has previously said: “We’re talking about at least one woman who was sent byJeffrey Epstein over to Prince Andrew.” Mr Edwards has added that after spending the night with the former prince, the woman says she was given tea and a tour of Buckingham Palace.

Detectives said they would speak to her only if she feels ready. They have told her lawyer that should she wish to report this to police, “it will be taken seriously and handled with care, sensitivity and respect for her privacy and her right for anonymity". The force added: “We recognise how difficult it can be to speak about experiences of this nature. Any contact with police will be led by her wishes, when and if she feels ready and able to do so.”

Article continues below

Virginia Giuffre, who accused him of abusing her in 2001, took her own life last April. She claimed that aged 17 she was trafficked by Epstein and his girlfriend Ghislaine Maxwell, and forced to have sex with Mountbatten-Windsor – which he denies. Speaking about the widened probe, Assistant Chief Constable Oliver Wright said: “Misconduct in public office is a crime that can take different forms, making this a complex investigation.

View 4 Images Andrew, who is now living at Marsh Farm, was arrested at nearby Wood Farm on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office (Image: PA)

"Our team of very experienced detectives are working meticulously through a significant amount ofinformation from the public and other sources. We are committed to conducting a thorough investigation into all reasonable lines of enquiry. We encourage anyone with information to get in touch with us through non-urgent channels, such as the Thames Valley Police online portal. The force is supporting national policing in contacting Epstein victims and survivors. It said: “We hope that anyone with relevant information will come forward whenever they are ready to engage with us.” Mountbatten-Windsor vehemently denies any wrongdoing.

News.title: Lee Andrews LIVE: Katie Price insists husband is still missing despite dad's arrest claim
News.content:
'Lee Andrews wanted to be paid to talk to me'

A sentence I never expected to type... I'd been exchanging messages with Lee since he married Katie in January. I'd been going to him for a right of reply on various stories I've been working on, with our first interaction regarding this story.

Last month, an ex-partner of Lee's, Crystal Janke, claimed he scammed her out of $150,000, so naturally, I sent him a message to see if he wanted to give a comment on the story. Another of Lee's exes also claimed to have had messages from Lee, claiming he was using an ex "to my advantage and played on her feelings".

But while the story came from another publication, Lee seemed to take issue and claimed that I was "paying" his ex-girlfriend for the story. I wasn't. His response was quite brutal, questioning why we would publish such allegations and not the "good things" people had said about him. "Good things," is a direct quote from Lee.

He wanted to be paid to share his side of the story, which I didn't agree to, so the conversation naturally ended.

News.title: Brighton beach women 'never recovered' after mum drowned - as heartbroken fourth sister organises funeral
News.content:
Brighton beach women 'never recovered' after mum drowned - as heartbroken fourth sister organises funeral

Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters, were found dead off Brighton beach earlier this month - it has since been revealed their mum died in similar circumstances

Flowers laid by a bench off Brighton beach where bodies of three women were recovered

Three sisters who died in a seaside tragedy never recovered from their mum's tragic death in similar circumstances.

‌



The bodies of Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32 and Rebecca Walters, 31, were pulled from the water off Brighton beach earlier this month. Relatives of the women, from Uxbridge, North West London, have reportedly said they had not known they were travelling to Brighton that morning, but had since reflected on whether they may have been marking the memory of their mother, who died by drowning in Birmingham, aged just 43.

‌



Now, the three women have left behind a devastated fourth sister. Lilly, a 25-year-old half sister, is reported to be inconsolable.

‌



Female family members are likely to organise the funeral, the Mail reported, with dad Joseph currently not having the strength to do so. Step-mum Genevieve Barnaby-Adetoro said she thinks it is "right" that Lilly, who lives in the US, is involved.

"We’ve said she can be in charge of their homecoming and she wants it to be as beautiful as possible, with white caskets and white roses," she said. "She even wants a carriage to take them home, to honour them. We will ask her to pick their clothes."

It is still not clear why the three women were in the water and Genevieve believes it possible they could not swim. Ajike Johnson, aunt to the three sisters, consoled Genevieve and said she was sure that they could.

‌



“Genevieve, you didn’t teach them, but they would have learned when they were young, before they lived with you," she said. “I’m sure they could swim… I remember Jane coming with us to that water park in Bolton when she came to stay. I’m sure she was swimming then.”

View 2 Images The family has spoken of their devastation after the incident (Image: Family Handout )

Sussex Police said there was no evidence to suggest criminality or that anyone else was involved, but specialist detectives are working to gather the full facts and circumstances around their deaths. Hundreds of hours of CCTV footage have been reviewed and inquiries made to businesses and properties around the beach area to try to track the women’s last movements, the force said.

‌



Emergency services were called after concerns were raised for a person’s welfare at around 5:45am on May 13, before three bodies were pulled from the water near Madeira Drive.

Thee three women were from the Uxbridge area of London.

Their father Joseph paid tribute to his three daughters “whose lives ended so tragically far too soon”.

‌



He said there are days when the grief feels “unbearable” but he holds onto the memories they shared and “the bond that death can never take away”.

A statement said: “Jane, Christina, and Becky were more than daughters to me; they were my joy, my strength, and the beautiful light that filled our family with happiness and love.

“Each of you was unique and precious in your own special way. Your smiles brightened dark days, your laughter brought comfort, and your presence made life more meaningful.

‌



View 2 Images Janice Adetoro (Image: BPM MEDIA)

“Though your time on earth was short, the impact you made will remain in our hearts forever.”

Genevieve revealed she and Joseph were watching the news at their home. Ajike said she was pinged a Sky News updates about the unfolding incident on her phone.

‌



Later, the police phoned and asked Joseph if he had children. When he said yes, officers arrived to inform them in person.

"We’d been watching the news and had no idea it was our girls," said Genevieve. "We didn’t even know they were in Brighton. Then we had to go and identify the girls, one by one."

The terrible incident has been a painful reminder of the death of mum Janice, who suffered from stress-related mental health problems before disappearing from her home in the Birmingham suburb of Erdington in the early hours of the morning. Reports suggest the tragedy happened in January 2012, but family members have said it took place in 2010.

‌



At the time, it was reported Janice lived with with two daughters, aged 15 and 20, and had a third daughter, aged 16, who lived with her father in Bedfordshire. At the time, Janice’s brother, Lincoln Walters said he had not heard from his sister since New Year’s Day, while her mum, Cynthia Smith-Walters, told how she had not seen Janice since their Christmas Day dinner.

Police said anyone with information regarding this month's incident is asked to come forward, particularly anyone who saw the sisters around the Madeira Drive area between 10pm on May 12 and 5.30am May 13.

Chief Superintendent Adam Hays said the force “will leave no stone unturned” in the investigation to understand what led to the “tragic events of that Wednesday morning”.

Article continues below

“The thoughts of everyone at Sussex Police are with the family of Jane, Christina and Rebecca following this devastating loss,” he said. “This investigation will continue in earnest, with Jane, Christina and Rebecca’s family at its centre. I would ask that they are given the privacy to come to terms with this terrible tragedy.”

Anyone with information can contact police online or via 101 quoting Operation Ledmore, serial 438 of 20/05.

An inquest into their deaths will open at Brighton coroner's court next Friday, May 29.

News.title: Heartbreaking tributes paid after 'kind and brilliant' teacher suddenly dies
News.content:
Heartbreaking tributes paid after 'kind and brilliant' teacher suddenly dies

Kevin Gahan, a popular teacher at Gorey Community School in Co Wexford, has sadly passed away. Colleagues and students have paid moving tributes to the beloved Enniscorthy educator.

View 4 Images Kevin Gahan

Touching tributes have flooded in for 'a true gentleman' and 'an inspiring teacher' following his death earlier this week.

‌



Kevin Gahan, hailing from Enniscorthy in Co Wexford, tragically died on Tuesday, May 19, with his loved ones sharing the devastating news via RIP.ie. "It is with deep sadness that we announce the tragic death of Kevin, on the 19th May 2026," the family statement read.

‌



"Deeply missed by his heartbroken family. Beloved husband of Elaine Dunne, parents Tom and Kath, brother Thomas, sister Elaine, brother in law Richie Murphy, sisters in law Mairead, Clodagh and Michelle, adored nephews Owen, Tomas, Pàidì and James and niece Mollie, parents in law Gay and Edel, the extended families, his many friends, his friends, colleagues and students in Gorey Community School to whom he was deeply committed and to the many people who knew and loved him."

‌



Mr Gahan, who wed his beloved Elaine last July, was a highly respected educator at Gorey Community School for several years, specialising in science, physics and biology. Numerous former colleagues have honoured the cherished teacher since news of his passing emerged, with many recalling him as a devoted professional who motivated both pupils and staff alike.

View 4 Images Kevin Gahan

One tribute stated: "So saddened to hear of Kevin's untimely death. I have fond memories of working with him in Gorey CS. A good colleague and an inspiring teacher.

‌



"Heartfelt sympathy to you Elaine on your inexpressible loss. Thinking also of the heartbroken Gahan and Dunne families at this time. May Kevin's gentle soul rest in peace."

A fellow staff member remarked: "Words cannot express how much Kevin will be missed. His passion for teaching and genuine kindness touched so many lives at GCS.

"It was a privilege to work with him. My deepest condolences to Elaine, the Gahan and Dunne families, his friends and colleagues. Ar dheis Dé go raibh a anam."

‌



View 4 Images Kevin Gahan

Another tribute read: "I had the pleasure of working with Kevin for many years and agree wholeheartedly with all the wonderful tributes that people have given. Along with having the privilege of working with him, he taught my son and I got to see first hand what so many students talk about," reports Dublin Live.

"He was one of a kind and went out of his way to encourage him. Thinking back, over the years I noticed a trend in our workplace, when ever someone spoke of him it was always with acknowledgement of what a lovely man he was. It always struck me when it happened that he was universally liked, and from the outpouring of condolence I see that it clearly extended beyond the workplace too.

‌



"To all of Kevin's family, my children and I are so sorry for the pain you are going through. Our prayers will be with you all."

A fourth colleague at Gorey Community School added: "Kevin was a wonderful teacher, but also a person of great integrity, compassion, and humour. He touched the lives of so many students and colleagues in GCS, and his kindness and wisdom will never be forgotten.

"My thoughts and prayers are with his beloved wife Elaine during this incredibly difficult time. My deepest sympathy to the Gahan and Dunne families. May they find comfort in the many lives he enriched and in the lasting memories he leaves behind.

‌



"He will be greatly missed by all who had the privilege of knowing him. Rest in Peace Kevin."

View 4 Images Kevin Gahan

Numerous former pupils of Kevin also paid heartfelt tribute to the Wexford-born educator, fondly recalling his dedication to teaching and the motivation he instilled in those under his tutelage. "Mr Gahan was a kind and brilliant teacher, who always strived to get the best out of his students, my classmates and I will always remember him as one of the best. May he rest in peace and god protect his family," one former student fondly recalled.

‌



Another mourner wrote: "Deepest sympathies to Elaine and all the Gahan and Dunne families. Kevin was a true gentleman. I loved going to his classes because he was so passionate about what he taught and his classes were always so interesting. It was also so touching to see his deep love for his wife. Rest in peace Mr Gahan."

A third tribute read: "My sincerest condolences to Elaine, and all of Kevin's family and friends. I have countless fond memories of Mr Gahan's physics class in room 216. He had such a genuine passion for teaching and always encouraged every student to fulfil their potential. He always went above and beyond when explaining concepts and carrying out experiments.

"One thing that always stood out to me was Mr Gahan's remarkable ability to recall where every past pupil sat in his lab throughout the years; a small detail which perfectly captured how much he cared for his students. His dry sense of humour made every class memorable, and I will never forget the kindness he showed me around the time of my Leaving Cert.

Article continues below

"I am deeply saddened to hear of his passing. He will be remembered fondly by so many whose lives he positively impacted. May he rest in peace."

The Gahan family have confirmed that details regarding his funeral arrangements are yet to be announced.

News.title: Armed police shoot man in Whitefield getaway bid as gun and drugs found
News.content:
Armed police shoot man in Whitefield getaway bid as gun and drugs found

Police pursuing a vehicle in Whitefield said the driver failed to stop and drove directly at officers to get away, before he was shot in the arm and taken to hospital

View 2 Images Forensic officers attend the scene in Whitefield (Image: Getty Images)

A man was shot by armed cops after he drove at them during a dramatic getaway attempt in Whitefield, with drugs and a gun later recovered by detectives.

Greater Manchester Police said officers tried to stop a car on Bury New Road at around 3pm on Friday, but the driver "failed to stop and drove directly at officers to get away". A firearms officer then discharged a weapon, striking the 20-year-old man in the arm.

He was taken to hospital with injuries described as neither life-threatening nor life-changing, while the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) later said he had suffered a suspected broken elbow.

Detectives later recovered drugs and a gun, and the man was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of Class A drugs, reports Manchester Evening News.

View 2 Images Forensic officers search the scene (Image: Getty Images)

In an update, GMP said an investigation into the incident is ongoing. The force said officers searched an address in Radcliffe overnight and found a firearm and a "significant" quantity of both Class A and Class B drugs. No further arrests have been made.

Detective Superintendent Joe Harrop, from GMP's Serious Crime Division said: "Our officers were met with an extremely dangerous situation on Bury New Road yesterday. Thankfully no members of the wider public, or officers were harmed in the incident.

"Despite this, our team has acted swiftly and professionally, and our investigation has progressed at pace. Overnight searches have led to the recovery of a firearm and a significant quantity of Class A and B drugs. This is a substantial find and it in turn prevents a potentially dangerous weapon and a significant amount of drugs from reaching our streets.

Article continues below

"Our investigation will progress, and we will continue to target those involved in serious and organised crime to keep our communities safe for all those who live and work across the whole of Greater Manchester."

In a statement issued this morning, the IOPC said: "We are independently investigating following a non-fatal police shooting in Bury. We were made aware by Greater Manchester Police, who advised that a man was shot in the arm after a vehicle failed to stop for officers. He was taken to hospital with a suspected broken elbow.

"While firearms incidents like this are, thankfully, rare, it is important for there to be independent scrutiny to fully understand what has happened. IOPC investigators attended the scene and to the police post-incident procedures to begin gathering evidence."

News.title: Hottest day of year so far as temperatures soar on bank holiday weekend
News.content:
Temperatures will continue to soar across the bank holiday weekend following the hottest day of the year so far on Saturday.

As of 16:00 BST, temperatures had reached 30.3C at Frittenden in Kent, beating the previous day's maximum temperature of 28.4C in London.

The heat is forecast to intensify throughout the long weekend, reaching heatwave criteria in a number of locations.

Daytime highs are forecast to reach the upper 20s Celsius in many areas, with the low 30s Celsius likely in the week ahead.

Amber heat health alerts remain in effect for the Midlands, eastern and south-east England.

Amber alerts mean there is a risk of a significant impact across health and social care services, with children and those aged over 65 at risk of negative health implications.

The remainder of England is under yellow heat health alerts, meaning adverse weather is "likely to affect vulnerable groups".

Charlton goalkeeper Sophie Whitehouse was the hero as she brilliantly saved four penalties in a 2-1 shootout victory over Leicester to earn promotion to the Women’s Super League.

Olivia McLoughlin scored ‌Leicester’s third spot-kick at the Valley to give ​her side hope, but ‌the 29-year-old Whitehouse ⁠capped a superb season between ⁠the sticks for Charlton by denying Leicester’s Heather ‌Payne ​and Noemie Mouchon to ‌win promotion for ​her side after a 0-0 draw following the first 120 minutes.

The WSL is expanding to 14 teams next season and by finishing third in WSL 2, Charlton earned a play-off against a Foxes side that finished bottom of the top flight, in a one-off game to decide who would grab the final spot.

open image in gallery Sophie Whitehouse was sensational in the penalty shootout ( Getty )

open image in gallery And Charlton were able to celebrate a hard-earned promotion to the WSL ( Getty )

The Addicks had looked to be cruising to automatic promotion from the second tier but picked up just one point from their final four matches to miss out on the final day of the regular season but picked themselves up to triumph in the play-off.

They will return to the top flight of women’s football for the first time since 2008, which came a year after the team was controversially temporarily disbanded despite having found success throughout the 2000s (including winning the FA Cup in 2005) because the men’s team had been relegated from the Premier League and the club were looking to cut costs.

It has been a long road back to the top for the Addicks and the tears from manager Karen Hills on the touchline after the game showed how much it meant.

Leicester were dismally out of form heading into the contest, having finished bottom of the WSL after a campaign that saw them lose every game since 14 December, and Rick Passmoor’s side are relegated after a five-year spell in the top flight. It compounds a dreadful season for the football club with the men’s side also relegated to League One.

open image in gallery Charlton will play top-flight football for the first time since 2008 ( Getty )

Charlton were the better team for large spells at the Valley and almost won it in extra-time when substitute Katie Lockwood’s thunderous strike was tipped on to the underside of the crossbar by Leicester stopper Katie Keane and the follow-up headed goal was disallowed for offside.

Whitehouse, the WSL 2 Golden Glove winner, had been brilliant between the sticks for Charlton as well, pulling off a stunning save to deny Shannon O'Brien on the stroke of half-time and blocking Ashleigh Neville’s back-post header in the 93rd minute.

After 120 goalless minutes, the game went to penalties and Ireland international Whitehouse ⁠rose to the occasion, saving the first two spot-kicks from Emily van Egmond and O’Brien, before plunging to her left to also deny Payne ​and Mouchon later in the shootout.

That meant Amalie Thestrup and Ellie Mason scoring two of Charlton’s four spot-kicks was enough to seal promotion to the promised land.

NASCAR champion Kyle Busch died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis, resulting in rapid and overwhelming complications, according to a statement from his family.

Busch died on Thursday, a day after he became unresponsive in a racing simulator. The two-time champion was 41 years old.

His family received the medical information Saturday, according to Dakota Hunter, vice president of Kyle Busch Companies.

Sepsis is a life-threatening medical emergency where the body's extreme response to an infection causes the immune system to damage its own tissues and organs, according to the CDC. This overactive response can lead to widespread inflammation, microscopic blood clots, and leaky blood vessels.

Busch had been preparing to race in Sunday’s Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte Motor Speedway when he collapsed during a test session in a Chevrolet racing simulator in Concord on Wednesday.

He was rushed to a hospital in Charlotte. An emergency call placed that afternoon described an individual with "shortness of breath, very hot, thinks he’s going to pass out, and is producing a little bit of blood, coughing up some blood."

open image in gallery An in memoriam photo of former driver Kyle Busch is displayed on the video board of the backstretch at Charlotte Motor Speedway, Friday, May 22, 2026 ( AP Photo/Matt Kelley )

The unidentified caller, whose audio was provided by the Cabarrus County Sheriff’s Office, stated Busch was lying on the bathroom floor but "he is awake," and requested that emergency responders arrive without sirens.

Earlier in May, Busch had reportedly suffered from a sinus cold while racing at Watkins Glen, radioing his team to request a "shot" from a doctor after the race.

Busch's illustrious career saw him secure 234 victories across NASCAR’s top three series, a record unmatched by any other driver in history. In tribute, all 39 drivers competing in Sunday’s race will display a black No. 8 decal on their cars.

Richard Childress Racing announced it will temporarily retire Busch’s car until Busch's 11-year-old son, Brexton, is old enough to take the wheel himself.

"Kyle Busch was instrumental in the design of RCR’s stylized No. 8 and it has become synonymous with Kyle and an important symbol for his fans and the NASCAR industry,” the team wrote.

“No one can carry it forward to the level that he did. The No. 8 is reserved and ready for Brexton Busch when he is ready to go NASCAR racing."

Richard Childress Racing has announced the temporary retirement of Kyle Busch’s iconic No. 8 Cup Series car following the unexpected death of the 41-year-old driver.

The team intends for the number to remain out of circulation until Busch's 11-year-old son, Brexton, is old enough to take the wheel himself.

Beginning with Sunday night's Coca-Cola 600, RCR will field the No. 33 car on the Cup Series circuit.

Austin Hill is slated to replace Busch, a two-time Cup Series champion, at Charlotte Motor Speedway for NASCAR's longest race of the season. Busch died unexpectedly on Thursday.

Busch died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis, resulting in rapid and overwhelming associated complications, according to a statement released by his family Saturday.

Brexton Busch is already making a name for himself in the racing world, having secured the Tulsa Shootout Jr. Sprint Championship last year, earning his first career Golden Driller trophy.

open image in gallery The late Kyle Busch and his son greet fans before a NASCAR Cup Series auto race at Talladega Superspeedway, April 23, 2023 ( AP Photo/Butch Dill )

In a poignant statement, RCR confirmed their decision: "Kyle Busch was instrumental in the design of RCR’s stylized No. 8 and it has become synonymous with Kyle and an important symbol for his fans and the NASCAR industry. No one can carry it forward to the level that he did. The No. 8 is reserved and ready for Brexton Busch when he is ready to go NASCAR racing."

A third-generation Busch driver, Brexton commenced his racing journey in 2020 at the age of five, competing in the Beginner Box Stock division at Millbridge Speedway in North Carolina.

His website details his first victory at Mountain Creek Speedway just a month later, and he has since amassed an impressive record, including 48 wins, 126 top-10s, and 107 top-5s across various race car styles in 2024.

This move echoes a previous decision by RCR in 2001, when the team changed car numbers from the black No. 3 to the white No. 29 after Dale Earnhardt's fatal crash at the Daytona 500.

The No. 3 eventually returned for the 2014 season, driven by owner Richard Childress's grandson, Austin Dillon.
